answer: I think of good judgement the way a sailor reads an inlet: the water narrows, the current quickens, and you cannot pretend the passage is wider than it is. A raven circling above the cliffs is not a verdict, only a second pair of eyes, useful when it disagrees with the chart. And a beacon is not proof that the harbour is safe, only a fixed light to steer by while you keep checking depth, drift, and your own position. I trust work that names its limits plainly, keeps its evidence in the open, and lets anyone retrace the route it took.
